newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, De Beers re-open diamond talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia, De Beers re-open diamond talks.

text.p: Russia and South African diamond group De Beers renewed talks on Tuesday on a new, three-year diamond deal, a company source said.
The source, who asked not to be identified, said the current round of negotiations was scheduled to last through Wednesday but could continue longer.

De Beers officials taking part in the talks were not available for comment, but the source said that the company's delegation was headed by Gary Ralfe, managing director of the firm's London-based Central Selling Organisation.
The talks, with Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS), which is Russia's largest diamond producer and sole authorised exporter, were being held at ARS's Moscow office.
De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd signed a memorandum with the Russian government in February giving it selling rights for one half of Russia's rough diamond output.
But a formal agreement with ARS, which must be reached for Russia to continue to sell its output on world markets through De Beers, has not yet been reached.

Russia's Committee for Precious Metals and Stones (Komdragmet), which formerly oversaw the domestic diamond industry, saw most of its responsibilities ceded to the finance and industry ministries under a government decree last week.
De Beers officials had said they did not know how or if the change would affect its talks with Russia.
